caption: Left: Relative share of the most frequent languages in the dataset. Right: Distribution of contributions among users.
model_annotation: This pie chart depicts the relative distribution of languages present in a dataset. The chart contains eight slices, representing English, Spanish, Russian, German, French, Chinese, and a combined “Other” category further specified as Catalan, Portuguese (Brazil), and Thai. The English slice is dark blue and occupies 42.8% of the chart, followed by the Spanish slice, also dark blue, at 31.4%. Russian is represented by a lighter blue slice at 5.7%, and German is a similar color at 3.6%. A light teal slice represents French at 2.9%, and a pale yellow slice represents Chinese at 1.9%. The “Other” category is a very light grey and occupies 5.8% of the chart, with individual labels for Catalan (1.6%), Portuguese (Brazil) (1.7%), and Thai (2.5%). Percentage labels are displayed within each slice. The slices are visually ordered in descending order based on their proportional size.
